summary: Unpinned github: dependency source resolves to author's personal fork on install
details: package.json declares the `libsignal` dependency as `github:Kelvdra/libsignal` — a bare git source pointing at the author's personal GitHub fork with no commit SHA, tag, or integrity hash. On `npm install`, this resolves and fetches the default branch of that repo at install time, executing any lifecycle scripts (preinstall/install/postinstall) contained in whatever the branch currently holds. This bypasses the npm registry's version-immutability guarantees: the code executed on the installer is whatever the repository owner (or anyone who compromises that GitHub account) pushes to the branch after publish. The package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library; a static match on a `ping` string in lib/Utils/generics.js appears in a generic keep-alive helper and is not an independent exfiltration signal.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
